results.title: KNOWN ISSUE: Support for Trial Access Pending or Denied Access
results.snippet:
We recognize that some developers are experiencing delays in the app-approval process for **trial access pending**, **upgrade to standard access pending**, or **trial access denials**. This topic is for providing instructions on how to get support.

**For account-specific help with Trial or Standard access, [submit a support ticket](https://help.pinterest.com/contact?pinterest_api_and_developer_tools=api_access&origin=pbc).**

Pinterest’s Developer Platform uses two access tiers to manage how apps interact with the API: Trial Access and Standard Access. Trial Access lets developers explore and test the API, but Pins and boards created through it are only visible to the app creator, not the public. Standard Access is intended for apps ready to launch to real users, offering full public visibility and higher rate limits, but it requires your app to already hold Trial Access and pass a review that includes a video demo of your app in action. For full details on both tiers, eligibility requirements, and the upgrade process, see [Understanding our access tiers](https://developer.pinterest.com/docs/key-concepts/access-tiers/) documentation.

This document describes a conceptual GraphQL schema for the Pinterest API v5. Pinterest is a visual discovery platform enabling users to save, organize, and discover ideas through images, videos, and links organized on boards. The REST API v5 covers pins, boards, users, advertising, catalogs, conversions, and analytics.
**Base REST API:** [https://api.pinterest.com/v5](https://api.pinterest.com/v5)
**Developer Documentation:** [https://developers.pinterest.com/docs/api/v5/](https://developers.pinterest.com/docs/api/v5/)
**GitHub:** [https://github.com/pinterest](https://github.com/pinterest)
---
## Schema Source
This GraphQL schema is derived from the Pinterest REST API v5 surface, translating resource endpoints and their data models into a unified GraphQL type system. Pinterest does not publish an official GraphQL API; this schema is a conceptual mapping intended for tooling, documentation, and integration planning.

The Pinterest API uses OAuth 2.0. Applications must obtain an access token with the appropriate scopes before making API calls. Available scopes include `pins:read`, `pins:write`, `boards:read`, `boards:write`, `ads:read`, `ads:write`, `catalogs:read

results.snippet:
# pinterest-mcp-server
A [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server for the **Pinterest API v5**.
**263 of Pinterest's 266 published operations** are reachable. The three that are not are the OAuth token endpoints, excluded for a security reason rather than an access one. A test compares the catalogue against Pinterest's own OpenAPI spec, so when Pinterest ships an endpoint the build goes red.
It keeps itself authorised (Pinterest tokens expire after 30 days; this refreshes them), and it can pin local images, carousels and videos from one folder you choose.
MIT licensed.
## Install
```
npm install -g @nasdigitaluk/pinterest-mcp
```
## Authorise once
Create an app at [developers.pinterest.com/apps](https://developers.pinterest.com/apps) and add `http://localhost:3034/oauth/redirect` as a redirect URI. Then:
```
PINTEREST_APP_ID=your-app-id PINTEREST_APP_SECRET=your-app-secret pinterest-mcp-auth
```
